title: A Fair Go for Australians in Trade Bill 2018
short_title: A Fair Go for Australians in Trade Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would constrain the contents of future Australian trade agreements and require independent assessments and broader consultation before agreements are signed.

It would prohibit labour market testing waivers, investor-state dispute settlement clauses and terms requiring public service privatisation or undermining pharmaceutical benefits and anti-dumping laws.
The rules would begin the day after Royal Assent and include protections for public welfare regulation and specified preferences in Commonwealth procurement arrangements.
changes: An independent national interest assessment would be commissioned and tabled before a proposed agreement is signed.
Bilateral agreements would need a labour chapter containing internationally recognised labour principles.
An accredited trade advisers program would provide consultation with unions, civil society and industry.
summary.affected: The Australian Government, employers seeking overseas workers, and union, civil society and industry trade advisers are affected.
